status: authored 2026-10-22 (offline: plan, generator, audit, pictures; NOTHING applied to any world, not seen in game)
owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-21: "with no caves people wont be incentivized to mine at all, it would be really nice to have some really really large and long mines every so often in the world" / "i need some to be thousands long or just somehow carve out caves underground, really need that" / "a few hunderd block caves wont be enoughfor 10 people" / "its looking more like 6 now"
design: Abandoned working mines cut into the rock under the hills of the eastern half (x >= 4096; the western half's natural caves are another builder's). Each network has a timbered adit, main haulage drifts with rails, crosscuts and long side drifts on several levels 16 blocks apart joined by stair inclines and ladder shafts, stopes where six players can work at once, and vanilla ore in the exposed walls. The ore is richer on the deeper levels and the farther from the adit. Everything is a hash of `seed` and the network id (tools/mines.py h32), grown on the canonical heightmap (tools/ground.py, rounded) and never on a world.

rules.x_min_why: the western half belongs to the natural-cave builder; stay at least 64 blocks east of x 4096
rules.river_corridor_why: data/water_shape.json rivers.defaults.corridor_half_width_blocks: the audit's footprint for a revised reach, so a meander may sit anywhere in it
rules.y_floor_min_why: the lowest floor, with its 2-block shell under it, stays well above the bedrock

ores.why: vanilla ores the bank buys (data/bank.json: coal, raw copper, raw iron, raw gold, lapis lazuli, redstone, diamond), placed in the exposed walls and roof of the drifts as veins that run back into the rock. `p` is the chance an exposed wall cell seeds a vein; it grows with the level (`depth_gain` per level below the first) and with the walk from the adit (`far_gain`, at 1500 blocks and beyond), and is multiplied in a stope. `y_max`: the highest floor a vein may seed at. Below y0 the deepslate variant is placed; from y0 to y7 a hash chooses.

networks.name: The Old Craters Drift
networks.reading: A long-abandoned coal and iron working under the hills north-west of Fossick, driven west from a timbered adit and followed down.

networks.name: The Hollow Seam
networks.reading: A copper and lapis seam followed north into the ridge above the gorge, abandoned when the lower levels flooded the miners' tempers, not their shafts.

networks.name: The Ridgeback Workings
networks.reading: The north-central highlands' oldest company working, driven south from a hillside adit and sunk level by level toward the iron.
